newsitem.title: INDIA: Shares end lower on India national exchange.
newsitem.headline: Shares end lower on India national exchange.

text.p: Share prices drifted lower on Monday at the National exchange with participants unwilling to make fresh commitments after a big fall on Wall Street, traders said.
"Very lacklustre," said one dealer at a big institutional brokerage house. "I can't see anyone building positions. People are concerned. They will stay on the sidelines."
A holiday at the rival Bombay bourse also contributed to the sluggish activity, he said.
The 50-share NSE index ends 23.95 pts, or 1.9 pct, lower at 1,203.95 provisional close.
Asian Paints bucked the trend after Britain's ICI Plc said it has bought a 9.1 percent stake.
The share rose 24.30 rupees, or 7.4 percent, to 353.80.
A Bombay-based finance firm Kotak Mahindra Capital Company said it had purchased the shares from the Choksey family, one of four original promoters of Asian Paints.
"Thereafter, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company has agreed to sell these shares to ICI Plc at 351 rupees per share subject to approvals," it said in a statement.
Asian Paints is ICI's main competitor in India.
Three other promoters have about 40 percent of Asian Paints' equity with Indian financial institutions and domestic investors holding another 40 percent, analysts said.
Analysts expect the market to open subdued on Tuesday.
"The Dow Jones tumble has affected the mood," said S.N. Satish, a fund manager at Lloyds Finance. "Fund managers are going to put fresh purchases on hold."
The market was unlikely to see a sell-off though, he said.
On Friday, the Dow Jones had slumped 247.37 points, or 3.1 percent, to 7,694.66 on a weakening dollar and worries on corporate earnings.
